'''Amenotakechi Shrine''' (あめのたけちじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Kashihara, Nara|Q496319|qid=Q496319}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=major shrine listed in the Engishiki}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was that of a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined Deities ===
Bold indicates the principal enshrined deity.
*'''{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611}}'''
*{{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803|lt=Okinaga-Tarashi-hime-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Himegami|Q22070227|qid=Q22070227}}

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
The date of foundation is unknown. The earliest appearance in historical records is an entry in the '''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}''' (see below). In the '''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}''', it is listed as a major shrine and is noted as receiving offerings at the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsukinami}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Niiname}} festivals.

From the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} through the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}, it was called Soga Hachimangū, and the enshrined deity was considered to be {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman Ōkami|qid=Q261637}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} in Meiji 40 ({{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}).

=== Divine Rank ===
* {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten’an}} 3 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) {{ill|January 27|Q2284|qid=Q2284}}: promoted from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ('''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}''') – recorded under the name “Amenotakechi no Kami”
